v: Terrific casting and makeup cannot rescue a film built almost entirely around mocking real people. RGV himself says audiences want entertainment — this is miles away from providing it.
e: Amma Rajyam Lo Kadapa Biddalu felt less like a movie and more like a long political spoof designed to ridicule a few people while glorifying another. The uncanny casting, makeup and imitations are genuinely impressive, but beyond that I found almost no story, emotion or entertainment to hold onto.
body:
I generally try to watch a movie simply as a movie and nothing else.

But here it was crystal clear to me that the entire exercise was created mainly to make a mockery of a few people and project one person as the greatest leader.

I had liked Lakshmi’s NTR because, irrespective of whom it was targeting politically, there was still a human story underneath it.

At its centre was the relationship between an aged, lonely man and an already-married woman, along with the consequences they faced because that man belonged to one of the most powerful political families.

There was something to engage with beyond the attack itself.

In Amma Rajyam Lo Kadapa Biddalu, I could not find that layer.

Most of the film felt like one spoof after another, with the audience simply being asked to recognise the real-life personalities being mocked.

The one department I genuinely appreciated was the casting and makeup.

The team does terrific work in making several actors resemble the personalities they are imitating, and the versions of Lokesh, Pawan Kalyan and K.A. Paul come surprisingly close in appearance and mannerisms.

But accurate imitation alone cannot carry an entire film.

RGV himself has a line in the movie saying that whether it is politics, cinema or life, the audience ultimately expects entertainment.

By that standard, this film fails its own argument.

For a general audience looking for an actual movie rather than a collection of political spoofs, it is far, far away from providing any real entertainment.

v: As the title suggests, it is Venky’s one-man show. His comedy, emotion and mama-alludu chemistry are the only real saving grace in an otherwise below-par film with a patience-testing climax.
e: Venky Mama survives almost entirely on Venkatesh’s effortless comedy and emotional timing and the chemistry between the uncle and nephew. The story, dialogue, direction, music and BGM leave little impression, while the pre-climax and climax become so illogical that even Venky’s charm cannot fully save the film.
body:
As the title itself suggests, this is Venky’s one-man show!!!

His comedy timing, emotional timing and the mama-alludu chemistry are easily the best things in the film.

Unfortunately, once you move beyond those elements, there is not much to say about the story, dialogues, direction, BGM or music.

None of those departments gives the film enough strength or identity of its own.

The pre-climax and climax are especially frustrating.

They stretch the audience’s patience with sequences that become completely illogical 🙏

Venkatesh keeps trying to lift the material through sheer warmth, timing and screen presence, and whenever he is in control the movie becomes noticeably more watchable.

But one performer can carry only so much.

Venky Mama himself is the saving grace for an otherwise below-par film.

v: LOVED IT!!!!!! Leave logic, emotion and message at home and this becomes a proper mad laugh riot. Akshay steals the show, even if my beloved Aakhri Pasta deserved much better 😄
e: Housefull 4 knows exactly what kind of movie it wants to be: loud, illogical and proudly ridiculous. It is neither the best nor the worst of the franchise, but Akshay Kumar’s expressions, the ensemble madness and a stream of absurd surprises made it a thoroughly enjoyable time-pass watch for me.
body:
LOVED IT!!!!!!

If you want a fun-filled, crazy movie and are completely willing to forget logic, this is exactly the kind of film that can work.

If you are going in expecting logic, deep emotions and a message… please stay at home 😄

I have followed both the Golmaal and Housefull franchises for years, and I would not call this the best entry in the series.

But it is definitely not the worst either.

Akshay Kumar is the real all-rounder of Bollywood.

He can move from action films to national-integrity dramas, message-oriented cinema and then jump straight into the complete madness of Housefull without looking uncomfortable for a second.

Here he steals the show with those epic facial expressions.

It also takes a certain confidence for a major star to accept a character that functions more like the film’s main comedian than a conventional HERO, and Akshay commits fully to the madness.

As a big fan of Aakhri Pasta, though, I was disappointed that the character was not etched as memorably as in the earlier Housefull films.

That was probably my biggest personal disappointment.

Beyond that, the film keeps throwing ridiculous surprises at you — including Nawazuddin Siddiqui turning up in an ITEM SONG and Hulk Rana becoming qawwali singer Rangeela Raja 🙏

Nothing here should be examined too seriously.

Overall, it is a nice time-pass laugh riot if you can surrender to the illogical plot and completely mad comedy!!!!!

v: The first 45 minutes are painful and familiar, but once the revolt begins Sye Raa transforms into a BLOCKBUSTER ride — Chiru’s eyes, dialogue diction and final stretch make the dream project come alive.
e: Sye Raa starts with a very familiar patriotic-film template and spends too long on family and romance, but the movie changes dramatically once its central conflict takes over. From there, Chiranjeevi, the huge supporting cast and the technical departments combine to deliver the scale, intensity and fan moments the opening stretch was missing.
body:
To start with, Sye Raa follows a very familiar patriotic-film structure.

Character introduction and early life, followed by oppression, revolt, backstabbing and then the end — the broad screenplay beats are all very recognisable.

To make matters worse, the first forty-five minutes were honestly painful for me.

There is too much focus on Narasimha Reddy’s family and romance, and the Chiranjeevi–Nayanthara–Tamannaah portions did not convince me at all.

But what follows that difficult opening stretch is what turns the movie around completely.

Once the central conflict is firmly established, Sye Raa becomes a BLOCKBUSTER experience.

From that point onwards it is a treat to watch the effort put in by the director, fight masters, dialogue writers, DOP and music team 🙏

A cast containing Chiranjeevi, Amitabh Bachchan, Kiccha Sudeep, Jagapathi Babu and Ravi Kishan gives the film enormous screen presence and helps carry the required intensity.

Yes, it can initially be difficult to imagine a sixty-plus Chiranjeevi physically as this warrior.

But then you look at the INTENSITY in his eyes and listen to the diction in those dialogues, and he convinces you to stop thinking about his age.

Acting-wise, for me this is among his best performances since Apadbandhavudu!!!!!

Surender Reddy’s direction becomes very strong once the story enters its main conflict, and he understands exactly when to give Chiru fans those big moments.

Special mention to the final ten minutes, which showcase Chiranjeevi’s intensity to the core 🙏

It was also good to finally see Tamannaah and Kiccha Sudeep receive substantial roles.

Tamannaah does very well, while Sudeep is excellent — he owns several scenes with that wonderfully careless attitude and at times even manages to dominate the frame opposite Chiru.

I was disappointed that Vijay Sethupathi was limited to only a couple of scenes because there was barely enough room for him to show what he can really do, although his screen presence still adds value.

Amitabh’s role is far more subtle as the guru.

But when performers of this calibre fill the screen together, it is simply an awesome sight.

In the end, the actors and technicians clearly put enormous effort into making Chiranjeevi’s dream project a SUCCESS.

If the opening forty-five minutes had been as strong as what follows, the impact could have been even bigger.
